acceptance: Codex tool_search requests, tool_search_call/tool_search_output history, additional_tools carriers, calls, and stream events round-trip across Responses and Chat without dropping IDs or client-execution semantics
additional_tools are consumed as structural metadata and their nested function/custom/namespace tools reach Chat without a null-content system/developer message
Unsupported server-side tools remain explicit safe field/direction errors; future unsupported tools expose only a bounded type discriminator in logs

A local upstream fixture that emits a Responses output event and then resets yields a protocol-level terminal error event with monotonic sequence_number, a failed request log, the actual upstream/downstream statuses, and a bounded failure phase
A reset before downstream headers remains a sanitized HTTP 502; a post-header stream reset is not mislabeled as a new wire-level 502
Native Responses passthrough withholds response.completed until clean transport EOF; missing terminal markers and upstream failure terminals cannot be logged as success
Responses sequence exhaustion and malformed upstream HTTP status are rejected safely before invalid frames or uncaught exceptions can escape
Each outbound attempt is pinned to the currently validated address set; a connection from an obsolete address set is not reused

When a validated upstream resolves to multiple approved addresses and an earlier address fails before the HTTP request is sent, the Gateway may use a later address; a local fixture proves a healthy later address receives exactly one model request
No automatic retry is made after ambiguous request transmission or partial output; logs never retain prompts, bodies, schemas, tool arguments, or credentials
The Codex placeholder clearly states what is and is not implemented and links to existing route/upstream/credential management without writing Codex config files
Full Runtime tests, Desktop tests, Desktop build, syntax/diff checks, and independent review pass with evidence
Both Res round trips preserve supported request controls and responses that contain text and tool calls; empty and failed upstream streams are recorded as failures and truncation is explicit

Streaming request logs record finite numeric upstream-header, first-byte, body-duration, chunk-count and Gateway-processing timings without retaining prompt or response content; a paced local SSE fixture proves the timing boundaries and old logs remain compatible in Desktop details

PR #22 targets master; current CI passes before merge; merge into master and synchronize the primary worktree; publish the next GitHub release v1.1.8 with verified installer, Portable, blockmap, and manifest assets matching their SHA-256 values. scope_revisions.source: User follow-up: recurring `HTTP 502 · upstream connection reset` despite a successful connectivity test and no provider-side usage log.
scope_revisions.decision: Add local-only coverage and safe fallback across already validated DNS addresses only while TCP/TLS connection establishment fails before request bytes can be sent. Do not retry after connection readiness, possible request transmission, response headers, or partial output. Keep provider-level reset cause unconfirmed without the provider's request trace.

scope_revisions.source: Independent backend review identified remaining native Responses passthrough, address-pool isolation, HTTP status validation, and sequence exhaustion edge cases.
scope_revisions.decision: Extend the same forwarding-resilience boundary to defer native response completion until clean EOF, fail closed on invalid/incomplete terminal streams and exhausted sequence space, isolate each upstream address attempt from cross-request socket pooling, and sanitize invalid HTTP response statuses. Keep all verification local and do not add post-send retries.
